question: What is the primary purpose of a two-way referral system in mental health care?

options.A: Minimizing the administrative workload of community nurses
options.B: Transferring chronic cases permanently to teaching hospitals
options.C: Ensuring continuity of care between different health tiers
options.D: Reducing the total population of psychiatric patients

explanation: A two-way referral system bridges community facilities and specialized centers to maintain uninterrupted patient management. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is the downward arm of a psychiatric referral system just as crucial as the upward arm?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for ongoing psychiatric nursing follow-up
options.B: It removes all legal liability from the tertiary psychiatric hospital
options.C: It ensures that primary health clinics can prescribe restricted psychotropic drugs
options.D: It prevents chronic overcrowding by moving stable patients back to community care

explanation: Downward referrals decongest tertiary facilities while keeping stable patients close to their social support networks. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which tier of the Nigerian healthcare system handles complex psychiatric disorders requiring specialist management?
explanation: Specialist psychiatric hospitals and teaching hospitals represent the tertiary tier for complex cases. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient presenting with acute psychotic symptoms in a remote rural community should first be managed at which facility level?
explanation: Initial contact and emergency stabilization typically occur at the nearest primary health center before formal referral upward. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which clinical finding strongly justifies an upward referral to a tertiary psychiatric facility?

options.A: Stable compliance with oral maintenance drugs
options.D: A desire for routine psychiatric counseling

explanation: High-risk behaviors like suicidal ideation exceed primary care capacity and require specialist psychiatric evaluation. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: What vital document must accompany a patient during an upward psychiatric referral?

options.A: A formal discharge certificate signed by a local government chairman
options.B: A detailed referral letter outlining patient history and treatments given
options.C: A court-mandated detention order for involuntary hospital admission
options.D: A comprehensive financial clearance receipt from the primary clinic

explanation: A written referral note ensures the receiving specialist team understands the baseline presentation and prior interventions. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of a downward mental health referral?

options.A: Punishing patients who refuse hospital admission
options.B: Reintegrating stabilized patients into community-based care
options.C: Permanently discharging patients from medical follow-up
options.D: Transferring financial costs away from the family

explanation: Downward referrals move stable individuals back to local facilities to promote recovery in familiar environments. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: What must be confirmed before a tertiary facility executes a downward referral for a chronic mental health patient?

options.A: Total financial independence of the patient's immediate family
options.B: Availability of maintenance psychotropic drugs at the local clinic
options.C: Construction of a specialized psychiatric ward at the primary center
options.D: Complete eradication of all psychiatric symptoms in the patient

explanation: Ensuring local drug availability prevents treatment interruption, which is a major driver of relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which task is a core responsibility of the psychiatric nurse during a referral process?

options.A: Manufacturing psychotropic medications for rural clinics
options.B: Legally transferring ownership of the community health center
options.C: Preparing the patient and family psychologically for the transition
options.D: Financing the patient's transportation to the tertiary hospital

explanation: Nurses play a central role in counseling patients and families to reduce anxiety associated with changing care facilities. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is nursing involvement in clinical handover critical during a psychiatric transfer?

options.A: To permanently close the patient file at the previous facility
options.B: To ensure the medical records department collects appropriate fees
options.C: To decide which doctor will head the tertiary management team
options.D: To accurately communicate behavioral risks and current stabilization status

explanation: Nurses observe daily behaviors and mental status changes, making their clinical handover essential for safe ongoing care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which factor represents a major operational barrier to downward referrals in many rural settings?

options.A: Over-digitization of all primary health center records
options.B: Excessive abundance of specialized psychiatric nurses
options.C: Strict government policies prohibiting patient transfers
options.D: Chronic stock-outs of essential psychotropic medications

explanation: Without reliable drug supplies at primary centers, clinicians cannot safely refer stabilized patients downward. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: How does societal stigma negatively impact the two-way referral system?

options.A: Tertiary facilities refuse to write comprehensive referral letters
options.B: Community health workers lack basic training in mental health screening
options.C: Hospitals are forced to discharge patients before clinical stability is achieved
options.D: Patients avoid local primary facilities and delay seeking early professional help

explanation: Stigma drives individuals away from local care, leading to advanced presentations that overwhelm tertiary centers. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of using standardized referral forms in psychiatric practice?

options.A: Completely eliminating the need for verbal nursing handovers
options.B: Automatically granting patients free access to all medications
options.C: Reducing the time patients spend waiting inside tertiary clinics
options.D: Ensuring critical clinical and behavioral information is consistently communicated

explanation: Standardized templates prevent omissions and give receiving clinicians a clear picture of the patient's history. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)

question: How can mobile health technology directly improve community psychiatric care in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Replacing the need for physical nursing assessments in all clinical cases
options.B: Eliminating transportation challenges by treating psychoses online
options.C: Automatically dispensing psychotropic drugs through mobile phones
options.D: Allowing remote primary nurses to consult specialists without patient travel

explanation: Mobile consultations bridge the geographical gap, enabling expert guidance for rural nurses managing complex cases. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)
